## Teaching points

1. Wernicke encephalopathy is not only an alcohol disease: hyperemesis gravidarum, bariatric surgery and any cause of malnutrition can deplete thiamine, and pregnancy increases demand.
2. The full triad of confusion, eye signs and ataxia is present in only a minority; the Caine criteria (two of dietary deficiency, eye signs, cerebellar signs, altered mental state or memory impairment) are more sensitive.
3. Treat on clinical suspicion with high-dose IV thiamine before glucose; do not wait for MRI or a thiamine level.
4. Typical MRI: symmetric T2-FLAIR signal in the medial thalami, mammillary bodies and periaqueductal gray, but a normal MRI does not exclude the diagnosis.
5. Standard prenatal vitamins contain only 1–2 mg of thiamine, too little for a patient with hyperemesis; supplement it early.
